rationale:
`src/execution_coverage/check.rs#fn[exceptions]` has an `errors: &mut Vec<String>` parameter, so it is a site of `requirements.ci.errors`. It meets the site obligations. Both violation matches are harmless.

- **`return Ok(BTreeMap::new())`**: this runs only when `crate::evidence::load_definitions` fails.
  - The failure is pushed into `errors` first.
  - Every check after it needs the definitions: `citation_items`, the review-path lookup and `validate_review`. None can run without them, so skipping them is allowed.
  - The only check independent of the definitions, `collect_references(root, errors)`, runs before the early return.
  - The caller `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#fn[check_saved]` still runs `discovered_files` and the per-file checks after `exceptions` returns. The failure therefore does not stop later independent checks.
- **`continue`**: this skips items that have no `habeas:coverage` citation. Such an item has no failed check to report, so nothing is skipped.
- **Later checks in the same loop iteration**: for each citation item, either `validate_review` runs or the "missing citation review" finding is pushed. These are exclusive branches of one check. The findings are then recorded in `accepted` and appended to `errors`. One failing item never prevents the next item from being checked.
- **Duplicate reporting**: each failure is pushed once. `check_saved` also removes duplicate messages from `errors` before printing, which guards against double reporting.

The `load_definitions` error text is a single joined message pushed as one error. That is a normal use of the convention. I found no gap.

text: Repository validation MUST continue after a failed check and report every failed
check it finds in one run, each as a {term}`requirements.ci.validation_error`.
This is a convention for every validation error; the requirement for each check
states which conditions that check reports. A file that cannot be parsed, such as
a malformed `habeas.toml`, `book.toml`, or evidence file, is one failed check:
its error MAY report only the first parse or decoding problem in that file, and
checks that do not depend on its contents MUST still run.
The code that sequences the repository's checks carries out the first paragraph.
A repository-validation function that collects validation errors MUST hold them
in a parameter or local variable named `errors`, and a function with such a
variable is a site below; authoring code that collects errors only to abort is
not one. After one of its checks fails, a site MUST still run every later check
that does not depend on the failed check's result, including later checks in the
same loop iteration, and MUST NOT report one failure twice.
One message in a repository validation report, describing a single failed check.
